sections.h2: What should a seller picture when thinking of Terrell County?
sections.html:
Think of 338 square miles of southwest Georgia farm country around a single city. Dawson holds the courthouse and is the only city, and Bronwood, Parrott and Sasser are the three towns. Wikipedia traces the county to February 16, 1856, with its name taken from William Terrell.

Ichawaynochaway Creek drains the western and southern two thirds, and the Kinchafoonee-Muckalee system takes the northeast. U.S. 82 is the main route, joined by State Routes 32, 41, 45, 49, 50, 55, 118 and 520. Webster, Sumter, Lee, Dougherty, Calhoun and Randolph counties form the borders.

Numbers are heading down. A 2020 census count of 9,185 became a July 2025 estimate of 8,656, a 5.7% slide from the Bureau's base. At roughly 27 residents per square mile, a parcel might be a farmhouse with acreage or a modest house on a Dawson street.

sections.h2: How do Terrell County's housing numbers read?
sections.html:
For 2020-2024 the Census Bureau puts $118,400 at the midpoint of what owners' homes are worth, and owners live in 61.6% of the occupied ones. Tenants face a midpoint gross rent of $745.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax paperwork in Terrell County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner sits at 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson. Letters go to P.O. Box 484, Dawson, GA 39842, and the tax website shows (229) 995-5151 with counter service from 8:00 AM until 4:30 PM on weekdays.

  • Tax commissioner, (229) 995-5151: statements, payments, penalties and levies.
  • Tax assessor, (229) 995-5210, P.O. Box 382: valuations, returns, homestead filings, mobile home registration.
  • Courthouse deed room: warranty deed copies.
  • Commissioners' office, (229) 995-4476: curbside trash for homes outside the four municipalities.

People who just bought are told to carry the warranty deed to the assessors when they apply for homestead, so collect it from the deed room first.

sections.h2: What is Terrell County's due date, November 15 or December 20?
sections.html:
Two county pages give different answers, so rely on the notice that reaches your mailbox. The general information page names December 20, while the FAQ states that bills for land, buildings and business equipment have come due November 15 since 2018. They agree on April 1 for mobile homes.

Late steps for land and buildings, as listed on the general information page:

  • Interest lands on the 2nd of each month, computed as prime plus 3% over twelve.
  • A FIFA lien is filed with the Clerk of Courts after 30 days have passed from the date on the delinquent notice.
  • A 5% penalty hits at 120 days and again every 120 days, stopping at 20%.
  • A file still open is handed to a collection firm, which tacks on administrative and levy charges that can reach $240.00 plus.

Those charges cover certified mail and a title search that readies the parcel for auction, and the property runs in the Herald Journal for four weeks first. By mail, a United States Postal Service postmark counts as on time, though a postage-meter stamp does not.

sections.h2: How are Terrell County mobile homes taxed?
sections.html:
Georgia classes a mobile or modular home as personal property. When one is in the county on January 1, the owner owes tax by April 1 and picks up a location permit at the same visit. Statements usually go out on January 2.

Missing April 1 draws a 10% penalty, and the county can send the owner to Magistrate Court or sell the home. On an overdue account, interest accrues on the 16th of each month, the penalty is applied April 2, and a FIFA is filed 30 days after the delinquent notice goes out. A decal must stay visible, and the assessors take questions at (229) 995-5210.

If a manufactured home is sold mid-year, find out which owner paid the permit tax before you set the closing.

sections.h2: What exemptions and appeal routes exist in Terrell County?
sections.html:
Terrell's assessors take homestead filings, and the home must be both owned and lived in on January 1. A form can come in at any time, yet it must land by April 1 to cover that year. After approval it continues until you move.

The tax website says Terrell County has local exemptions, and a local figure replaces the state one whenever it is larger. Ask the assessors for current amounts. Owners 62 and older may qualify for more relief. A deferral program lets those owners with gross household income of $15,000 or less delay payment until ownership changes or deferred tax and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

Farm land can be assessed at 30 percent in place of 40, and Conservation Use values land on its actual use. Both ask for a covenant of ten years or more.

An appeal must start no later than 45 days after the notice, citing taxability, value or uniformity. Unresolved cases go on to the equalization board or an arbitrator, then Superior Court. For an owner on armed forces duty, a friend or relative can file within 90 days.

sections.h2: Do Terrell County business owners file returns too?
sections.html:
Yes. Personal property returns on form PT-50p go to the Board of Assessors every year, no matter whether value or use has changed. The tax site warns that an owner who no longer has a listed item must say so or stay on the roll for it, and that skipping a required real estate return costs 10% of the value left off.

Business equipment, machinery and fixtures are assessed at 40 percent of market value. Manufacturers can seek the freeport exemption for raw goods, goods in process, or finished goods held for shipment out of state, filing between the first of January and April 1.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes before selling in Terrell County?
sections.html:
Phone (229) 995-5151 and request a written balance for every year, mobile home accounts included. Find out whether a FIFA sits on record at the superior court clerk's office, because a lien has to be paid off for a deed to record cleanly.

Georgia fixes value on the first day of January, so the commissioner can describe how the year of your sale will be billed. Tell the title company about each open item early. A lien that surfaces at the closing table pushes the date out, and accounts that reached the collection stage cost more, since the added charges sit on top of the balance.

A cash buyer who accepts the property in its present condition can pay these amounts from your proceeds and close without repairs.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Terrell County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: (229) 995-5151. The office is at 187 E. Lee Street in Dawson and opens at 8:00 AM and closes at 4:30 PM on weekdays. Mail goes to P.O. Box 484.

faqs.q: Is Terrell County's due date November 15 or December 20?
faqs.a: The county pages disagree: general information says December 20 and the FAQ says November 15 beginning in 2018. Follow the date shown on your own statement.

faqs.q: What is the Terrell County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year you want the exemption. Apply with the assessors, and bring your deed if you recently bought.

faqs.q: How soon must I appeal a Terrell County assessment?
faqs.a: No later than 45 days after the notice. Valid grounds are taxability, value or uniformity, and a complaint about the amount of tax is not one of them.

faqs.q: What if I skip a Terrell County tax payment?
faqs.a: Interest starts the 2nd of the following month, a FIFA lien follows 30 days after the delinquent notice, and a 5% penalty builds every 120 days up to 20%. A long unpaid account is passed to a collection firm and can end in a sale.
